Issued at 300 AM CST Sat Nov 21 2026

Unseasonably Mild and Dry Again Today... 

A strong upper level ridge was over the Eastern US into the
eastern Great Lakes while deep upper level trof was over the
Rockies/Western States with cutoff 529 decameter 500 mb low 
over southwest Saskatchewan province and strong upper level 
trof over Utah and near NV/AZ border. A 1028 mb surface high 
pressure was along the eastern PA/NY border and ridging sw 
across KY/TN. An elongated surface low extended from northern MN
sw thru eastern NE to 1005 mb low in southeast CO. In between 
these features, expect breezy south to SSW winds to bring 
another day of unseasonably mild highs in the lower 70s with a 
fair amount of sunshine with some passing cirrus clouds. Lincoln
and Peoria were only one degree shy of their record highs 
yesterday, and a few cities will be approaching record highs 
today like Galesburg. Lows overnight in the upper 40s/lower 50s,
with some mid 40s near the Wabash river.

Wet Sunday, Turning Colder Sunday Night Into Next Week... 
A pair of strong shortwaves digging out of the southern 
Canadian Prairies and another across Utah are forecast to phase
as they move east across the mid and upper Mississippi Valley 
on Sunday. This to push the cold front east into far nw CWA by
dawn Sunday morning and moving into pushing across central 
IL Sunday morning and through southeast IL during Sunday
afternoon. There is a fetch of deeper moisture lifting into this
system from the western Gulf and PW peak from 1-1.25 inches in
narrow band on Sunday. Models continue to show a widespread 
band of light to moderate rain showers spreading into the IL
river valley by early Sunday morning and into southeast IL early
Sunday afternoon, with showers diminishing in southeast IL
during early Sunday evening. Instability remains weak keeping 
thunderstorm chances minimal. Overall QPF is expected to be 
light between a tenth and quarter inch with pockets of a half to
three quarter inches mainly west of highway 51. This will offer
minimal relief for the ongoing regional drought. Highs Sunday 
range from mid to upper 50s over the IL river valley (coolest in
Knox and Stark counties) to 65-70F in southeast IL, mildest in 
Lawrence county). Breezy NW winds 15-25 mph behind the cold 
front to see temperatures slipping about 10 degrees by sunset, 
into the mid to upper 40s nw of the IL river and 55-60F in 
southeast IL.

A 1035 mb Canadian high pressure to build se across the upper
Midwest/northern Great Plains Sunday night and further into the
Midwest on Monday and over the Great Lakes region Tue. 
Much colder air arrives on north/nw winds Sunday night and
Monday. Lows Sunday night around 30F over central IL and 32-35
from I-70 southeast. Despite ample sunshine Monday, it will be
seasonably cold with highs in the mid to upper 40s in central 
IL and lower 50s from highway 50 south. Nearby high pressure 
ridge to maintain dry weather Monday through at least Wed 
morning along with continued seasonably cold conditions. Lows
Monday and Tue night in the low to mid 20s with highs Tue and
Wed in the low to mid 40s with partly sunny skies Tue as clouds
increase from the west Tue morning. Temps a bit below normal
during mid week to only slightly modify Thanksgiving weekend
with highs in the mid 40s Thanksgiving Day and mid to upper 40s
Fri/Sat and lows in the 20s.

Medium range forecast models continues to signal a storm system
impacting the Ohio river valley Wed afternoon into Friday. Still
appears brunt of moisture/qpf is east of IL with this storm
system Thu Wednesday into Thursday with NBM pops 20% or less in
eastern IL. There still remains substantial spread among model 
guidance, though consensus and trends are further east of IL 
with more widespread QPF which could also have snow chances with
the rain. Thanksgiving holiday travelers should continue to 
monitor forecasts especially if heading out east of IL toward 
the eastern Ohio river valley and New England.

The Climate Prediction Center (CPC) 8-14 Day Outlook for Nov
28-Dec 4th has a 50-60% chance of above normal temperatures 
over central/se IL, with precipitation trending near normal. 
CPC Week 3-4 Outlook for Dec 5-18th (released Nov 20th) has 
35-50% chance of above normal temperatures over CWA (greater
than 50% in northern IL), and equal chances of above or below 
normal precipitation over CWA.
